display: Pack-house supervisor at an export rose farm on Lake Naivasha. About two tonnes of export-rejected stems a week go into our compost pit, and I'm looking for a better use for them.

signals.text: About two tonnes of export-rejected stems (short, bent, bruised) go into our compost pit every week, because the Dutch buyer won't take them.
The compost pit is nearly full and smells, and the farm needs a plan for the rejects before the rainy season.
A co-worker's cousin dries rejected petals and sells them as potpourri at the market. I'd like to know whether that could work at farm scale.
I counted roughly 25,000 stems a week going into the pit. If even a third could be used, it would matter.
I want to find out who could use fresh or dried rose stems and petals, such as craft, cosmetics, food, dye, packaging or biogas.
The Valentine's early shipment starts on 1 November and we need volume. The grading lines are running slow and the workers are tired.
Our rejection rate has crept up this month, and I'm trying to work out why line three has so many bruised petals.
Cold room and handling practice for reducing bruising on a grading line is something I'd like to compare notes on.
A road washout has doubled my commute, so my days are long and I leave home at 4:30 am.
I'm learning a new Kikuyu hymn with my church choir, and the alto line is tricky.
I'm after practical, low-cost ways to earn a bit of extra income alongside my shifts, using what I know about flowers and compliance.

offers.text: I supervise a pack-house of 140 workers across three grading lines for weekly export to Amsterdam, and I can explain how it runs.
I know flower grading standards: sorting by stem length, bud size and quality, then bunching and boxing for the Dutch auction.
I know cold chain handling for cut flowers.
I know EU residue and phytosanitary record-keeping and what buyers' agents ask for.
I can quantify the reject stream (volume, stem lengths, defect types) and arrange samples from a steady weekly supply, with the farm's agreement.
I have contacts in the farm's quality and agronomy teams and a good reputation with the Dutch buyers' agents.
I can train and organise a line of workers quickly to sort or pre-process material.
I sing alto in a church choir and can join or help a community choir.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I make dried-flower products (potpourri, sachets, tea blends, natural dye) and need a steady supply of petals and stems in Kenya. Do you know where to get them?
catchers.can: Wanjiru can describe the weekly reject volume and quality, and take the idea to the farm's management and quality team, who decide commercial terms. She cannot commit the farm herself.
catchers.confirm: Could you use petals or stems that failed export grading (short, bent or lightly bruised) in volumes of hundreds of kilos a week, collected near Naivasha?

catchers.hypo: I run a biogas or composting operation and want rose and other flower waste as feedstock. Is there a farm near Lake Naivasha with a surplus?
catchers.can: She can confirm the volume and how it is handled today, and introduce the person on the farm who could agree to a pilot.
catchers.confirm: Can you collect about two tonnes a week from a farm gate and handle the transport yourself?

catchers.hypo: I'm a researcher or startup working on products from floriculture waste (extracts, fibre, pigment). Can we get samples of reject stems and the spray history of each batch?
catchers.can: Wanjiru can arrange samples through the farm. Through agronomist Peter she can ask for batch spray and residue records, once the farm agrees and the relationship is trusted.
catchers.confirm: Do you need documented spray and residue history for the material, and are you able to sign an agreement with the farm before receiving samples?

catchers.hypo: I'm a flower-farm quality manager and my rejection rate has risen. Which handling steps on a grading line most affect bruising?
catchers.can: She can share practical checks on cold room temperature, line speed and handling, and compare notes.
catchers.confirm: Are you asking about post-harvest handling and grading on an export pack-house line, rather than field agronomy or growing?

catchers.hypo: I'm a buyer or compliance officer for cut flowers and want to understand how a Kenyan farm keeps EU residue records for every bed.
catchers.can: She can explain how the records are organised and used. Her agronomist colleague Peter keeps the underlying spray records.
catchers.confirm: Is your question about how pack-house and bed-level records are kept and checked, rather than a request to see a specific farm's records?

catchers.hypo: I run a small enterprise in Naivasha and want to hire people with pack-house experience for seasonal work. Who do you know?
catchers.can: She can point to experienced line workers and supervisors she trusts, after checking they are free of farm commitments.
catchers.confirm: Is this seasonal or part-time work in the Naivasha area that does not clash with export-farm shifts?

catchers.hypo: Our choir needs an alto for a Kikuyu hymn programme in Naivasha. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: Wanjiru can sing alto herself, and her choir leader can connect your choir to others nearby.
catchers.confirm: Is this a church or community choir that rehearses on evenings or weekends in or near Naivasha?

forbids.text: I cannot speak for farm management on commercial decisions such as pricing, contracts or releasing material.
I do not share the farm's spray and residue records with strangers before the farm agrees and trust is established.
I cannot take on work during my pack-house shift (5am to 3pm, longer in peak season).
I will not cut corners on EU compliance or traceability.
I only work around Naivasha and cannot travel far.

projects.name: Reject stem disposal
projects.text: Find a use for about two tonnes a week of export-rejected rose stems and petals, currently going into a compost pit that is nearly full.
roles_needed: natural dye, cosmetics or food ingredient maker

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, I will share production and quality details: reject volumes, defect types, handling and cold chain practice.
policy.t2: When fit is clear and the farm has agreed, I will share spray and residue records for the relevant beds, including the rejects.
policy.never: I never share personal finances, my family's private details, or anything about my job security.
